_source: Wikipedia article summaries fetched 2026-09-05; entries marked approximate:true are from general knowledge where no article was available.

alma-mater.title: Alma Mater
facts: Three figures: Alma Mater with arms outstretched before a throne; Learning and Labor clasp hands behind her.
About 13 ft of bronze weighing 10,000 lb, on a granite base at Green and Wright.
Restored 2012–2014, when laser cleaning returned it from green patina to bronze.

illini-union.title: Illini Union
facts: The campus home for student organisations, at the north head of the Main Quad.
Red brick with a white portico, dormers and an octagonal clock cupola.
Built with a Public Works Administration grant plus a loan repaid through student fees.

foellinger.title: Foellinger Auditorium
facts: A 120 ft diameter circular hall of brick and Indiana limestone on a granite foundation.
The dome was re-clad in copper in the 1983–85 renovation and carries 396 embedded lights.
Closes the south end of the Main Quad, facing the Illini Union.

altgeld.title: Altgeld Hall
facts: The 132 ft chime tower holds 15 bells weighing 7.5 tons, played from a wooden chimestand.
Grey rusticated stone with a red tile pyramid roof and four corner turrets.
Home to the only gargoyle on campus.

siebel.title: Siebel Center for Computer Science
facts: 225,000 sq ft across four floors, funded in part by alumnus Thomas Siebel.
Built as a ‘computing habitat’: sensor-driven locks, proximity awareness and intelligent building systems.
Glass curtain wall with a copper-clad drum on the north end.

eceb.title: Electrical & Computer Engineering Building
facts: Designed as a net-zero-energy building, with a rooftop solar array and terracotta rain-screen fins.
Glass-fronted lobby and second-floor balcony over the atrium.
Anchors the north edge of the engineering campus on Wright Street.

grainger.title: Grainger Engineering Library
facts: Five levels and over 92,000 sq ft; the main reading gallery seats 1,254.
A concave brick facade with a curved skylight runs along the Bardeen Quad.
Its 1994 ribbon-cutting was entirely digital — a touchscreen triggered on-screen fireworks.

dcl.title: Digital Computer Laboratory
facts: Housed ILLIAC, among the first computers built at a university.
Connected to Siebel by a bridge walkway.
Still home to Computer Science teaching space and the CS loading dock.

kenney.title: Kenney Gym
facts: The old men’s gymnasium on Springfield Avenue, now used for events and recreation.
One of the largest open floors on the engineering side of campus.
The HackIllinois main hall and bleacher seating.

stadium.title: Memorial Stadium
facts: Nearly 200 stone columns line the east and west facades, each engraved with the name of a fallen Illinois student or alumnus.
A U-shaped bowl open to the south, with double-decked sideline stands; capacity 60,670.
The playing field is Zuppke Field, with Illini-orange end zones.

state-farm.title: State Farm Center
facts: Opened as Assembly Hall; the largest dome structure in North America until the Astrodome in 1965.
The folded concrete roof is held by 614 miles of quarter-inch steel wire wrapped around its base.
15,544 permanent seats; the warm light under the rim is the concourse.

main-library.title: Main Library
facts: Anchor of one of the largest public university library collections in the world.
Red brick and limestone in the same Georgian language as the Union.
Sits south of the Main Quad on Gregory Drive.

beckman.title: Beckman Institute
facts: Founded with a $40M gift from Arnold and Mabel Beckman plus $10M from the state.
One of the first research centres in the world dedicated to interdisciplinary science.
Roughly 200 faculty and 500 graduate students work across intelligent systems, imaging and molecular science.

krannert.title: Krannert Center for the Performing Arts
facts: Four venues: Foellinger Great Hall (2,078 seats), Tryon Festival Theatre, Colwell Playhouse and the Studio Theatre.
The lobby floor is Thai teak that cost $1M; the walls are Carrara marble.
The Great Hall has no parallel surfaces, so instrumental music needs no amplification.
